conflicts.point: Whether strict post-market liability provides a stronger deterrent against algorithmic bias and deployment harms than pre-market compliance checklists.

positions.stance: Post-market strict liability attaches direct responsibility to operating principals, preventing actors from hiding behind regulatory safe harbor stamps.
Post-market checks arrive too late to prevent irreversible systemic failures, making upfront verifiable boundaries necessary.

verdicts.conflict: Whether strict post-market liability provides a stronger deterrent against algorithmic bias and deployment harms than pre-market compliance checklists.
verdicts.rationale: Both positions highlight valid governance challenges. The safetyist position accounts for irreversible systemic risks from frontier models, while the skeptic position points to documented, real-world harms in current enterprise deployments.
